title: The Super Bus
paragraphs: Everyone notices the high-tech changes that are happening to our personal automobiles, with GPS systems now a standard feature and cars that drive themselves coming soon. But some companies are also working on developing high-tech bus systems. Most recently, the first ever 'Super bus' is being developed by a Dutch company. The company is run by Wubbo Ockels, who is a former astronaut and the creator of the amazing super bus.

What makes the bus so 'super'? First of all, it's very fast. It has a top speed of 250 kph (155 mph). In order to travel that fast, the bus will run on special roads. However, unlike a train, which must always use rail lines, the super bus can also travel on normal roads at normal speeds. This means the bus can travel quickly between cities like a train, but take passengers to specific destinations within the city, like a normal bus. When it travels on the special high-speed highway, it travels very low – only 7 cm off the ground. This helps the super bus travel faster and remain more stable, but of course it can only travel that low on a special highway. When it moves onto normal city streets, it moves to a more typical height of 43 cm.

Knowing how fast it is, you may be surprised to learn that the super bus is powered by electricity. It can travel 200 km on a single battery. When the bus has gone 200 km, it will make a quick stop so the driver can switch batteries. The battery has been designed so that it's very easy for any person to pull out and replace quickly.

The super bus looks like a very long sports car, very luxurious – more like a limousine than a bus. It is 15 meters long (50 feet). There are eight doors on each side of the bus that lift up, giving the bus a futuristic look. The interior can be arranged in different ways, with seats in rows, or facing each other to form a 6-person compartment.

Several places have shown interest in the super bus, including Dubai, Abu Dhabi and the Netherlands. Ockels hopes to have the buses on the roads by 2016, so keep your eyes open for super buses in a city near you!
